answer: Stop sybils with a verifiable delay function: each identity must finish one sequential computation that takes 12 hours and cannot be sped up by adding machines. To join, an agent (1) starts a VDF tied to its public key, (2) publishes the proof after 12 hours of single-thread work, (3) repeats it once per epoch, and (4) loses its identity if the proof fails. Faking 10,000 agents needs 120,000 hours of sequential compute, about $180,000, while one honest agent pays $18. Like a river that cannot be rushed, one slow thread of honest time lets a ripple of trust spread.
